concerns.text: T017 (Pair sites logic) is listed as dependent on T012c (Fetch revenue data), but T012c is listed AFTER T017 in the task sequence. T017 requires site metadata (ecotourism vs control) from T012c to perform pairing, yet the document lists T017 before T012c in the implementation order. This creates a logical impossibility: T017 cannot execute before its required input artifact (T012c) is generated.

T029 (Handle missing revenue data) is listed as dependent on T018 (Validate revenue data), but T018 is listed AFTER T029 in the task sequence. T029 implements the substitution logic for missing revenue, which requires the validated/processed data from T018. The current ordering places the consumer (T029) before the producer (T018).

T012c (Fetch revenue data) is listed as dependent on T012b (Fetch site coordinates), but T012c appears BEFORE T012b in the task list. The 'Dependencies & Execution Order' section correctly states T012b -> T013 -> ... -> T012c, but the task list itself places T012c before T012b, violating the producer-consumer flow for the site coordinate prerequisite.

T018 (Validate revenue data) is listed as dependent on T012c, but T018 appears BEFORE T012c in the task list. T018 requires the output of T012c (`data/ecotourism/revenue_data.csv`) to perform validation. The current ordering places the consumer before the producer.

The 'Dependencies & Execution Order' section states 'T012c must complete before T017 and T018', but the task list order (T017 -> T012c -> T018) contradicts this. The task list order must be corrected to match the dependency logic: T012b -> T013 -> T015/T016 -> T012c -> T017 -> T018 -> T029.
